topic: Class Template Specialization and Inheritance in C++
explanation: In C++, class templates enable the creation of generic classes that can operate with different data types. When combined with inheritance, templates allow for flexible and reusable class hierarchies that can adapt to various types and behaviors. This is particularly useful in the Standard Template Library (STL) and in designing complex, type-safe abstractions. Modern C++ enhances this with features like default template parameters, explicit specializations, and type traits, enabling highly customizable and efficient code.
syntax: template <typename T, typename U = DefaultType> class ClassName : public BaseClass<T> { /* class members */ };
example_explanation: This example defines a class template 'MyStream' that inherits from 'std::basic_istream', parameterized by character type and traits, demonstrating how class templates can be specialized with default template parameters and inheritance. In 'main', it creates an instance of 'MyStream' with a character stream buffer, showcasing how templates enable creating flexible, type-safe stream classes that extend standard library components with custom behavior, exemplifying modern C++ template programming and inheritance.
